traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Tropaeolaceae: leaves usually alternate, sometimes opposite; leaves simple or compound; compound leaves palmate; veins palmate; stipules present or absent; leaf rosettes none; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup present; stems herbaceous; flowers solitary; flowers zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit schizocarp or drupe, rarely samara; stamens 8; carpels 3. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Tropaeolaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 352, 354, family Tropaeolaceae: leaf incision none to palmately lobed or divided, usually; read as {"lobed": "often", "none": "often"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Tropaeolaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually tubers. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
